content.description: Build a fresh release APK via `cargo make build-android` so the 5 spawn_local-fixed files reach the device.

content.subject: Install APK on Pixel 10 Pro XL
content.description: adb install -r the new APK on device 57231FDCQ008Y4 (Pixel 10 Pro XL, Android 16).

content.subject: Paste user-provided invitation code, verify room joins
content.description: Skipped — `cargo make build-android` ships with `--features example-data`, so the on-device app uses hardcoded sample rooms (Public Discussion Room with Karen/Nacho) instead of network-joined rooms. The user-provided invite code therefore can't be used through this APK. Verification of crash flows proceeded against the example-data rooms instead, which exercises the same UI code paths the invite-joined rooms would hit.

content.subject: Verify member-info modal focus (was crash path)
content.description: Verified on Pixel 10 Pro XL. User opened the member-info modal; no SIGABRT, no "cannot access imported statics" panic. The `member_info_modal.rs:181` onmounted-focus call now routes through `crate::util::safe_spawn_local` and executes cleanly.

content.subject: Verify DM compose flow (was crash path)
content.description: Verified on Pixel 10 Pro XL. User opened DM thread (line 940 onmounted-focus path), composed and sent a message (line 524 compose flow), and opened the delete-confirm dialog (also line 940). No SIGABRT and no "cannot access imported statics" panic. All three `crate::util::safe_spawn_local` swaps in dm_thread_modal.rs execute cleanly.

content.subject: Verify nickname-edit blur (was crash path)
content.description: Verified that the spawn_local fix itself doesn't crash. The blur-on-Enter site at `nickname_field.rs:197` was never reached on device because a DIFFERENT pre-existing crash (GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed at dioxus-signals-0.7.9/src/global/mod.rs:100:46) fires earlier in the save chain. That crash is unrelated to spawn_local — filed separately. The spawn_local edit at line 197 is statically verified (cargo check clean on host + wasm32) and isolated to a code path that didn't execute because of the earlier panic.

content.subject: Wire Android clipboard via JNI (Copy buttons are no-ops)
content.description: Verified on Pixel 10 Pro XL after building + installing the patched APK: user confirmed "The Copy button works!" The JNI bridge in `ui/src/util.rs::android_copy_to_clipboard` (mirrors the `node_runtime::android_files_dir` pattern — pull JavaVM+Activity from ndk_context, attach thread, reflect Context.getSystemService("clipboard") → ClipData.newPlainText → setPrimaryClip) correctly writes the text into the system clipboard, where the user could paste it. Pre-fix behaviour was a no-op `let _ = text;` that silently swallowed every Copy.

content.subject: Fix GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed in nickname-save chain
content.description:
Pre-existing crash surfaced during Android verification on Pixel 10 Pro XL. Panic at `dioxus-signals-0.7.9/src/global/mod.rs:100:46` ("called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: AlreadyBorrowed(AlreadyBorrowedError)") on a nickname edit + Enter.

Sequence from logcat (`/tmp/claude/river-logcat.txt`, line 5569):
1. `Sending PutRequest for room MemberId(K53VLDBK)` (room_synchronizer.rs)
2. `Saving rooms to delegate storage` (chat_delegate.rs)
3. `Serialized request payload size: 131383 bytes`
4. Panic — `thread 'main' (4707) panicked at .../global/mod.rs:100:46`
5. SIGABRT

`nickname_field.rs::save_changes` already wraps its `ROOMS.with_mut` in `crate::util::defer`, so the immediate save delta is safe. The re-entrant borrow must be in the downstream chain triggered by `mark_needs_sync(owner_key)` — likely `save_rooms_to_delegate` reading a GlobalSignal while another mutation is still borrowed. Audit `save_rooms_to_delegate` and any use_effect / use_memo it triggers for unwrapped GlobalSignal reads (per AGENTS.md "Always use try_read()" rule).

Reproduction: edit a nickname in member-info modal, press Enter on Android (Pixel 10 Pro XL, current build). Unverified if web is affected.
content.activeForm: Pending: GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed in nickname save

content.subject: Move misleading "Saving nickname changes" log into closure body
content.description:
`nickname_field.rs:60` has `info!("Saving nickname changes");` inside the closure-creation block (around `let save_changes = { info!(...); ... move |new_value| { ... } }`), so it fires on every component re-render — i.e. every keystroke in the nickname input — not on actual saves. The 30+ log entries we saw in the verification logcat were all spurious re-renders, not actual save attempts.

Fix: move the `info!` inside the `move |new_value: String| { ... }` block so it only fires when `save_changes(new_value)` is actually called from `on_blur` or `on_keydown(Enter)`. Cosmetic but the noise actively obscures real save activity in logs (and confused the initial diagnosis of the GlobalSignal crash above).

content.subject: Verify rename + dark-mode on device
content.description: Verified end-to-end on Pixel 3a API 34 emulator after committing 3f07803 (rename + dark mode) and the followup icon commit. Probe via injected JS showed pcs:true, metas:1, bg:rgb(10,10,11) — confirming `prefers-color-scheme: dark` matches and the body bg is the `--color-bg: #0a0a0b` token from tailwind.css's dark block. Visual screencap of "Welcome to River" page shows full dark theme. Launcher label reads "River" (notification permission dialog, All Apps drawer). Adaptive icon shows the dolphin logo.

content.subject: Investigate: rooms multiply on every Android launch
content.description:
Root cause: `example_data::create_room` generates fresh random `SigningKey`s every call, so `initial_rooms()` produced new owner_vks per launch. The chat-delegate save+load path persisted those random keys and merged them with the next launch's fresh set — same name, different HashMap key, both kept. 4 launches → 12 entries.

Fix committed: in `ui/src/components/app/chat_delegate.rs`, under `cfg(feature = "example-data")`, skip both `fire_load_rooms_request().await` in `set_up_chat_delegate` AND early-return `Ok(())` from `do_save_rooms_to_delegate`. Example-data builds now keep ROOMS purely in-memory per session.

Verified on Pixel 3a API 34 emulator: fresh install + 3 cold launches → exactly 3 rooms each time (Public Discussion Room, Team Chat Room, Your Private Room).

content.subject: Verify DM compose flow (was crash path)
content.description: Verified on Pixel 10 Pro XL. User opened DM thread (line 940 onmounted-focus path), composed and sent a message (line 524 compose flow), and opened the delete-confirm dialog (also line 940). No SIGABRT and no "cannot access imported statics" panic. All three `crate::util::safe_spawn_local` swaps in dm_thread_modal.rs execute cleanly.

content.subject: Verify nickname-edit blur (was crash path)
content.description: Verified that the spawn_local fix itself doesn't crash. The blur-on-Enter site at `nickname_field.rs:197` was never reached on device because a DIFFERENT pre-existing crash (GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed at dioxus-signals-0.7.9/src/global/mod.rs:100:46) fires earlier in the save chain. That crash is unrelated to spawn_local — filed separately. The spawn_local edit at line 197 is statically verified (cargo check clean on host + wasm32) and isolated to a code path that didn't execute because of the earlier panic.

content.subject: Wire Android clipboard via JNI (Copy buttons are no-ops)
content.description: Verified on Pixel 10 Pro XL after building + installing the patched APK: user confirmed "The Copy button works!" The JNI bridge in `ui/src/util.rs::android_copy_to_clipboard` (mirrors the `node_runtime::android_files_dir` pattern — pull JavaVM+Activity from ndk_context, attach thread, reflect Context.getSystemService("clipboard") → ClipData.newPlainText → setPrimaryClip) correctly writes the text into the system clipboard, where the user could paste it. Pre-fix behaviour was a no-op `let _ = text;` that silently swallowed every Copy.

content.subject: Fix GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed in nickname-save chain
content.description:
Pre-existing crash surfaced during Android verification on Pixel 10 Pro XL. Panic at `dioxus-signals-0.7.9/src/global/mod.rs:100:46` ("called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: AlreadyBorrowed(AlreadyBorrowedError)") on a nickname edit + Enter.

Sequence from logcat (`/tmp/claude/river-logcat.txt`, line 5569):
1. `Sending PutRequest for room MemberId(K53VLDBK)` (room_synchronizer.rs)
2. `Saving rooms to delegate storage` (chat_delegate.rs)
3. `Serialized request payload size: 131383 bytes`
4. Panic — `thread 'main' (4707) panicked at .../global/mod.rs:100:46`
5. SIGABRT

`nickname_field.rs::save_changes` already wraps its `ROOMS.with_mut` in `crate::util::defer`, so the immediate save delta is safe. The re-entrant borrow must be in the downstream chain triggered by `mark_needs_sync(owner_key)` — likely `save_rooms_to_delegate` reading a GlobalSignal while another mutation is still borrowed. Audit `save_rooms_to_delegate` and any use_effect / use_memo it triggers for unwrapped GlobalSignal reads (per AGENTS.md "Always use try_read()" rule).

Reproduction: edit a nickname in member-info modal, press Enter on Android (Pixel 10 Pro XL, current build). Unverified if web is affected.
content.activeForm: Pending: GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed in nickname save

content.subject: Move misleading "Saving nickname changes" log into closure body
content.description:
`nickname_field.rs:60` has `info!("Saving nickname changes");` inside the closure-creation block (around `let save_changes = { info!(...); ... move |new_value| { ... } }`), so it fires on every component re-render — i.e. every keystroke in the nickname input — not on actual saves. The 30+ log entries we saw in the verification logcat were all spurious re-renders, not actual save attempts.

Fix: move the `info!` inside the `move |new_value: String| { ... }` block so it only fires when `save_changes(new_value)` is actually called from `on_blur` or `on_keydown(Enter)`. Cosmetic but the noise actively obscures real save activity in logs (and confused the initial diagnosis of the GlobalSignal crash above).

content.subject: Verify rename + dark-mode on device
content.description: Verified end-to-end on Pixel 3a API 34 emulator after committing 3f07803 (rename + dark mode) and the followup icon commit. Probe via injected JS showed pcs:true, metas:1, bg:rgb(10,10,11) — confirming `prefers-color-scheme: dark` matches and the body bg is the `--color-bg: #0a0a0b` token from tailwind.css's dark block. Visual screencap of "Welcome to River" page shows full dark theme. Launcher label reads "River" (notification permission dialog, All Apps drawer). Adaptive icon shows the dolphin logo.

content.subject: Investigate: rooms multiply on every Android launch
content.description:
Root cause: `example_data::create_room` generates fresh random `SigningKey`s every call, so `initial_rooms()` produced new owner_vks per launch. The chat-delegate save+load path persisted those random keys and merged them with the next launch's fresh set — same name, different HashMap key, both kept. 4 launches → 12 entries.

Fix committed: in `ui/src/components/app/chat_delegate.rs`, under `cfg(feature = "example-data")`, skip both `fire_load_rooms_request().await` in `set_up_chat_delegate` AND early-return `Ok(())` from `do_save_rooms_to_delegate`. Example-data builds now keep ROOMS purely in-memory per session.

Verified on Pixel 3a API 34 emulator: fresh install + 3 cold launches → exactly 3 rooms each time (Public Discussion Room, Team Chat Room, Your Private Room).

If a panic does fire, RUST_BACKTRACE=1 will name the offender — fix the missed callsite and retry.

No SIGABRT and no "cannot access imported statics" panic. All three `crate::util::safe_spawn_local` swaps in dm_thread_modal.rs execute cleanly.

content.subject: Verify nickname-edit blur (was crash path)
content.description: Verified that the spawn_local fix itself doesn't crash. The blur-on-Enter site at `nickname_field.rs:197` was never reached on device because a DIFFERENT pre-existing crash (GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed at dioxus-signals-0.7.9/src/global/mod.rs:100:46) fires earlier in the save chain. That crash is unrelated to spawn_local — filed separately. The spawn_local edit at line 197 is statically verified (cargo check clean on host + wasm32) and isolated to a code path that didn't execute because of the earlier panic.

content.subject: Wire Android clipboard via JNI (Copy buttons are no-ops)
content.description: Verified on Pixel 10 Pro XL after building + installing the patched APK: user confirmed "The Copy button works!" The JNI bridge in `ui/src/util.rs::android_copy_to_clipboard` (mirrors the `node_runtime::android_files_dir` pattern — pull JavaVM+Activity from ndk_context, attach thread, reflect Context.getSystemService("clipboard") → ClipData.newPlainText → setPrimaryClip) correctly writes the text into the system clipboard, where the user could paste it. Pre-fix behaviour was a no-op `let _ = text;` that silently swallowed every Copy.

content.subject: Fix GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed in nickname-save chain
content.description:
Pre-existing crash surfaced during Android verification on Pixel 10 Pro XL. Panic at `dioxus-signals-0.7.9/src/global/mod.rs:100:46` ("called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: AlreadyBorrowed(AlreadyBorrowedError)") on a nickname edit + Enter.

Sequence from logcat (`/tmp/claude/river-logcat.txt`, line 5569):
1. `Sending PutRequest for room MemberId(K53VLDBK)` (room_synchronizer.rs)
2. `Saving rooms to delegate storage` (chat_delegate.rs)
3. `Serialized request payload size: 131383 bytes`
4. Panic — `thread 'main' (4707) panicked at .../global/mod.rs:100:46`
5. SIGABRT

`nickname_field.rs::save_changes` already wraps its `ROOMS.with_mut` in `crate::util::defer`, so the immediate save delta is safe. The re-entrant borrow must be in the downstream chain triggered by `mark_needs_sync(owner_key)` — likely `save_rooms_to_delegate` reading a GlobalSignal while another mutation is still borrowed. Audit `save_rooms_to_delegate` and any use_effect / use_memo it triggers for unwrapped GlobalSignal reads (per AGENTS.md "Always use try_read()" rule).

Reproduction: edit a nickname in member-info modal, press Enter on Android (Pixel 10 Pro XL, current build). Unverified if web is affected.
content.activeForm: Pending: GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed in nickname save

content.subject: Move misleading "Saving nickname changes" log into closure body
content.description:
`nickname_field.rs:60` has `info!("Saving nickname changes");` inside the closure-creation block (around `let save_changes = { info!(...); ... move |new_value| { ... } }`), so it fires on every component re-render — i.e. every keystroke in the nickname input — not on actual saves. The 30+ log entries we saw in the verification logcat were all spurious re-renders, not actual save attempts.

Fix: move the `info!` inside the `move |new_value: String| { ... }` block so it only fires when `save_changes(new_value)` is actually called from `on_blur` or `on_keydown(Enter)`. Cosmetic but the noise actively obscures real save activity in logs (and confused the initial diagnosis of the GlobalSignal crash above).

content.subject: Verify rename + dark-mode on device
content.description: Verified end-to-end on Pixel 3a API 34 emulator after committing 3f07803 (rename + dark mode) and the followup icon commit. Probe via injected JS showed pcs:true, metas:1, bg:rgb(10,10,11) — confirming `prefers-color-scheme: dark` matches and the body bg is the `--color-bg: #0a0a0b` token from tailwind.css's dark block. Visual screencap of "Welcome to River" page shows full dark theme. Launcher label reads "River" (notification permission dialog, All Apps drawer). Adaptive icon shows the dolphin logo.

content.subject: Investigate: rooms multiply on every Android launch
content.description:
Root cause: `example_data::create_room` generates fresh random `SigningKey`s every call, so `initial_rooms()` produced new owner_vks per launch. The chat-delegate save+load path persisted those random keys and merged them with the next launch's fresh set — same name, different HashMap key, both kept. 4 launches → 12 entries.

Fix committed: in `ui/src/components/app/chat_delegate.rs`, under `cfg(feature = "example-data")`, skip both `fire_load_rooms_request().await` in `set_up_chat_delegate` AND early-return `Ok(())` from `do_save_rooms_to_delegate`. Example-data builds now keep ROOMS purely in-memory per session.

Verified on Pixel 3a API 34 emulator: fresh install + 3 cold launches → exactly 3 rooms each time (Public Discussion Room, Team Chat Room, Your Private Room).

If a panic does fire, RUST_BACKTRACE=1 will name the offender — fix the missed callsite and retry.

content.content:
1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	#
3	# Apply River's Android overlay to the dx-generated module.
4	#
5	# dx (the Dioxus CLI) regenerates the Android module — manifest,
6	# MainActivity stub, etc. — every build. The Dioxus-managed way to add
7	# our own Kotlin code and tweak the manifest is to (a) keep the canonical
8	# files in `ui/android/`, and (b) re-apply them on top of the generated
9	# tree right before gradle assembles the APK. This script does (b).
10	#
11	# What it does (idempotent — safe to re-run on every build):
12	#   1. Copies every file under `ui/android/kotlin/` into the dx-generated
13	#      `src/main/kotlin/` directory, overwriting the stubs dx wrote there.
14	#   2. Patches `AndroidManifest.xml` to:
15	#      - Add `FOREGROUND_SERVICE` permission (INTERNET is already added
16	#        by dx).
17	#      - Add `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC` permission (required on
18	#        API 34+ for the `dataSync` foregroundServiceType; ignored on
19	#        older OS versions).
20	#      - Declare `<service android:name="dev.dioxus.main.RiverNodeService"
21	#        android:foregroundServiceType="dataSync" />` inside the
22	#        `<application>` element. `dataSync` is the closest stock
23	#        foreground-service type for a P2P node's background sync work
24	#        and is the only one compatible with the dx-generated
25	#        `compileSdk = 33`. If the project ever bumps compileSdk to 34+
26	#        we can switch to `specialUse` with a `freenet_p2p_node` subtype.
27	#
28	# The script writes only to `target/dx/`. It never touches `ui/android/`
29	# (the source-of-truth overlay) or anything outside the dx-generated
30	# Android module.
31	
32	set -euo pipefail
33	
34	# Where dx writes the Android module. Mirrors the path in
35	# `Makefile.toml`'s build-android task.
36	ANDROID_MODULE_DIR=${ANDROID_MODULE_DIR:-target/dx/river-ui/debug/android/app}
37	OVERLAY_DIR=${OVERLAY_DIR:-ui/android}
38	
39	if [[ ! -d "$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR" ]]; then
40	    echo "ERROR: dx-generated Android module not found at $ANDROID_MODULE_DIR" >&2
41	    echo "       Run 'cargo make build-android' once to generate it, then re-run this script." >&2
42	    exit 1
43	fi
44	
45	if [[ ! -d "$OVERLAY_DIR" ]]; then
46	    echo "ERROR: overlay source dir not found at $OVERLAY_DIR" >&2
47	    exit 1
48	fi
49	
50	MANIFEST="$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml"
51	if [[ ! -f "$MANIFEST" ]]; then
52	    echo "ERROR: AndroidManifest.xml not found at $MANIFEST" >&2
53	    exit 1
54	fi
55	
56	echo "Applying River Android overlay…"
57	echo "  Overlay source:  $OVERLAY_DIR"
58	echo "  Module target:   $ANDROID_MODULE_DIR"
59	
60	# 1. Copy overlay Kotlin / resources into the generated module.
61	#    `cp -R` preserves the directory layout (so dev/dioxus/main/*.kt
62	#    lands at src/main/kotlin/dev/dioxus/main/*.kt).
63	if [[ -d "$OVERLAY_DIR/kotlin" ]]; then
64	    cp -R "$OVERLAY_DIR/kotlin/." "$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/src/main/kotlin/"
65	    echo "  ✓ Copied Kotlin overlay"
66	fi
67	if [[ -d "$OVERLAY_DIR/res" && -n "$(ls -A "$OVERLAY_DIR/res" 2>/dev/null)" ]]; then
68	    # For every file in our overlay tree, remove any same-basename file
69	    # in the target that has a DIFFERENT extension. Android's resource
70	    # merger treats `ic_launcher.png` and `ic_launcher.webp` in the same
71	    # density bucket as duplicates of the `ic_launcher` resource and
72	    # fails the build. The dx-generated tree ships defaults as .webp,
73	    # but a prior overlay run that placed .png files will leave them in
74	    # the target on subsequent builds (dx doesn't clean). This sweep
75	    # makes the overlay self-healing — pruning stale variants before
76	    # copying our canonical extension.
77	    while IFS= read -r -d '' overlay_file; do
78	        rel="${overlay_file#$OVERLAY_DIR/res/}"
79	        rel_dir=$(dirname "$rel")
80	        full_base=$(basename "$rel")
81	        base="${full_base%.*}"
82	        ext="${full_base##*.}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Apply River's Android overlay to the dx-generated module.
#
# dx (the Dioxus CLI) regenerates the Android module — manifest,
# MainActivity stub, etc. — every build. The Dioxus-managed way to add
# our own Kotlin code and tweak the manifest is to (a) keep the canonical
# files in `ui/android/`, and (b) re-apply them on top of the generated
# tree right before gradle assembles the APK. This script does (b).
#
# What it does (idempotent — safe to re-run on every build):
#   1. Copies every file under `ui/android/kotlin/` into the dx-generated
#      `src/main/kotlin/` directory, overwriting the stubs dx wrote there.
#   2. Patches `AndroidManifest.xml` to:
#      - Add `FOREGROUND_SERVICE` permission (INTERNET is already added
#        by dx).
#      - Add `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC` permission (required on
#        API 34+ for the `dataSync` foregroundServiceType; ignored on
#        older OS versions).
#      - Declare `<service android:name="dev.dioxus.main.RiverNodeService"
#        android:foregroundServiceType="dataSync" />` inside the
#        `<application>` element. `dataSync` is the closest stock
#        foreground-service type for a P2P node's background sync work
#        and is the only one compatible with the dx-generated
#        `compileSdk = 33`. If the project ever bumps compileSdk to 34+
#        we can switch to `specialUse` with a `freenet_p2p_node` subtype.
#
# The script writes only to `target/dx/`. It never touches `ui/android/`
# (the source-of-truth overlay) or anything outside the dx-generated
# Android module.

set -euo pipefail

# Where dx writes the Android module. Mirrors the path in
# `Makefile.toml`'s build-android task.
ANDROID_MODULE_DIR=${ANDROID_MODULE_DIR:-target/dx/river-ui/debug/android/app}
OVERLAY_DIR=${OVERLAY_DIR:-ui/android}

if [[ ! -d "$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR" ]]; then
    echo "ERROR: dx-generated Android module not found at $ANDROID_MODULE_DIR" >&2
    echo "       Run 'cargo make build-android' once to generate it, then re-run this script." >&2
    exit 1
fi

if [[ ! -d "$OVERLAY_DIR" ]]; then
    echo "ERROR: overlay source dir not found at $OVERLAY_DIR" >&2
    exit 1
fi

MANIFEST="$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml"
if [[ ! -f "$MANIFEST" ]]; then
    echo "ERROR: AndroidManifest.xml not found at $MANIFEST" >&2
    exit 1
fi

echo "Applying River Android overlay…"
echo "  Overlay source:  $OVERLAY_DIR"
echo "  Module target:   $ANDROID_MODULE_DIR"

# 1. Copy overlay Kotlin / resources into the generated module.
#    `cp -R` preserves the directory layout (so dev/dioxus/main/*.kt
#    lands at src/main/kotlin/dev/dioxus/main/*.kt).
if [[ -d "$OVERLAY_DIR/kotlin" ]]; then
    cp -R "$OVERLAY_DIR/kotlin/." "$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/src/main/kotlin/"
    echo "  ✓ Copied Kotlin overlay"
fi
if [[ -d "$OVERLAY_DIR/res" && -n "$(ls -A "$OVERLAY_DIR/res" 2>/dev/null)" ]]; then
    # For every file in our overlay tree, remove any same-basename file
    # in the target that has a DIFFERENT extension. Android's resource
    # merger treats `ic_launcher.png` and `ic_launcher.webp` in the same
    # density bucket as duplicates of the `ic_launcher` resource and
    # fails the build. The dx-generated tree ships defaults as .webp,
    # but a prior overlay run that placed .png files will leave them in
    # the target on subsequent builds (dx doesn't clean). This sweep
    # makes the overlay self-healing — pruning stale variants before
    # copying our canonical extension.
    while IFS= read -r -d '' overlay_file; do
        rel="${overlay_file#$OVERLAY_DIR/res/}"
        rel_dir=$(dirname "$rel")
        full_base=$(basename "$rel")
        base="${full_base%.*}"
        ext="${full_base##*.}"
        target_dir="$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/src/main/res/$rel_dir"
        if [[ -d "$target_dir" ]]; then
            for stale in "$target_dir/$base".*; do
                if [[ -f "$stale" && "${stale##*.}" != "$ext" ]]; then
                    rm "$stale"
                fi
            done
        fi
    done < <(find "$OVERLAY_DIR/res" -type f -print0)
    cp -R "$OVERLAY_DIR/res/." "$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/src/main/res/"
    echo "  ✓ Copied res overlay (pruned stale duplicate-extension variants)"
fi

# 2. Patch the manifest. Each insertion is idempotent — we grep for
#    the entry first and only add if missing. This means re-running the
#    script after dx has regenerated a fresh manifest produces the same
#    result as running it the first time.
patch_manifest() {
    local pattern=$1
    local before=$2
    local insertion=$3

    if grep -q -F "$pattern" "$MANIFEST"; then
        return 0
    fi

    # Insert `$insertion` on the line BEFORE `$before`. macOS sed needs
    # the -i '' form; we use a portable Perl invocation instead so the
    # script runs the same on macOS and Linux CI.
    perl -i -pe "s|($before)|$insertion\n\$1|" "$MANIFEST"
}

# Add FOREGROUND_SERVICE + FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC permissions.
# We grep-test for each by full string so re-runs are no-ops.
patch_manifest \
    'android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE"' \
    '<application ' \
    '    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE" />'
patch_manifest \
    'android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC"' \
    '<application ' \
    '    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC" />'

# POST_NOTIFICATIONS is required on API 33+ for the foreground-service
# notification to be visible in the status bar. Without it the FGS still
# runs (Android allows the process to keep executing) but the user sees
# nothing — defeating the "ongoing presence" UX of the service.
# This is a runtime permission too: the user must grant it on first
# launch. The MainActivity overlay requests it via PermissionHelper.
patch_manifest \
    'android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS"' \
    '<application ' \
    '    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS" />'

# Declare the service inside <application>. Inserted on the line BEFORE
# `</application>` so the closing tag remains intact.
patch_manifest \
    '"dev.dioxus.main.RiverNodeService"' \
    '</application>' \
    '        <service android:name="dev.dioxus.main.RiverNodeService" android:exported="false" android:foregroundServiceType="dataSync" />'

echo "  ✓ Patched AndroidManifest.xml"
echo "Overlay applied successfully."

content.description: adb install -r the new APK on device 57231FDCQ008Y4 (Pixel 10 Pro XL, Android 16).

content.description: Skipped — `cargo make build-android` ships with `--features example-data`, so the on-device app uses hardcoded sample rooms (Public Discussion Room with Karen/Nacho) instead of network-joined rooms. The user-provided invite code therefore can't be used through this APK. Verification of crash flows proceeded against the example-data rooms instead, which exercises the same UI code paths the invite-joined rooms would hit.

content.subject: Verify member-info modal focus (was crash path)
content.description: Verified on Pixel 10 Pro XL. User opened the member-info modal; no SIGABRT, no "cannot access imported statics" panic. The `member_info_modal.rs:181` onmounted-focus call now routes through `crate::util::safe_spawn_local` and executes cleanly.

content.subject: Verify DM compose flow (was crash path)
content.description: Verified on Pixel 10 Pro XL. User opened DM thread (line 940 onmounted-focus path), composed and sent a message (line 524 compose flow), and opened the delete-confirm dialog (also line 940). No SIGABRT and no "cannot access imported statics" panic. All three `crate::util::safe_spawn_local` swaps in dm_thread_modal.rs execute cleanly.

content.subject: Verify nickname-edit blur (was crash path)
content.description: Verified that the spawn_local fix itself doesn't crash. The blur-on-Enter site at `nickname_field.rs:197` was never reached on device because a DIFFERENT pre-existing crash (GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed at dioxus-signals-0.7.9/src/global/mod.rs:100:46) fires earlier in the save chain. That crash is unrelated to spawn_local — filed separately. The spawn_local edit at line 197 is statically verified (cargo check clean on host + wasm32) and isolated to a code path that didn't execute because of the earlier panic.

content.subject: Wire Android clipboard via JNI (Copy buttons are no-ops)
content.description: Verified on Pixel 10 Pro XL after building + installing the patched APK: user confirmed "The Copy button works!" The JNI bridge in `ui/src/util.rs::android_copy_to_clipboard` (mirrors the `node_runtime::android_files_dir` pattern — pull JavaVM+Activity from ndk_context, attach thread, reflect Context.getSystemService("clipboard") → ClipData.newPlainText → setPrimaryClip) correctly writes the text into the system clipboard, where the user could paste it. Pre-fix behaviour was a no-op `let _ = text;` that silently swallowed every Copy.

content.subject: Fix GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed in nickname-save chain
content.description:
Pre-existing crash surfaced during Android verification on Pixel 10 Pro XL. Panic at `dioxus-signals-0.7.9/src/global/mod.rs:100:46` ("called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: AlreadyBorrowed(AlreadyBorrowedError)") on a nickname edit + Enter.

Sequence from logcat (`/tmp/claude/river-logcat.txt`, line 5569):
1. `Sending PutRequest for room MemberId(K53VLDBK)` (room_synchronizer.rs)
2. `Saving rooms to delegate storage` (chat_delegate.rs)
3. `Serialized request payload size: 131383 bytes`
4. Panic — `thread 'main' (4707) panicked at .../global/mod.rs:100:46`
5. SIGABRT

`nickname_field.rs::save_changes` already wraps its `ROOMS.with_mut` in `crate::util::defer`, so the immediate save delta is safe. The re-entrant borrow must be in the downstream chain triggered by `mark_needs_sync(owner_key)` — likely `save_rooms_to_delegate` reading a GlobalSignal while another mutation is still borrowed. Audit `save_rooms_to_delegate` and any use_effect / use_memo it triggers for unwrapped GlobalSignal reads (per AGENTS.md "Always use try_read()" rule).

Reproduction: edit a nickname in member-info modal, press Enter on Android (Pixel 10 Pro XL, current build). Unverified if web is affected.
content.activeForm: Pending: GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed in nickname save

content.subject: Move misleading "Saving nickname changes" log into closure body
content.description:
`nickname_field.rs:60` has `info!("Saving nickname changes");` inside the closure-creation block (around `let save_changes = { info!(...); ... move |new_value| { ... } }`), so it fires on every component re-render — i.e. every keystroke in the nickname input — not on actual saves. The 30+ log entries we saw in the verification logcat were all spurious re-renders, not actual save attempts.

Fix: move the `info!` inside the `move |new_value: String| { ... }` block so it only fires when `save_changes(new_value)` is actually called from `on_blur` or `on_keydown(Enter)`. Cosmetic but the noise actively obscures real save activity in logs (and confused the initial diagnosis of the GlobalSignal crash above).

content.subject: Verify rename + dark-mode on device
content.description: Verified end-to-end on Pixel 3a API 34 emulator after committing 3f07803 (rename + dark mode) and the followup icon commit. Probe via injected JS showed pcs:true, metas:1, bg:rgb(10,10,11) — confirming `prefers-color-scheme: dark` matches and the body bg is the `--color-bg: #0a0a0b` token from tailwind.css's dark block. Visual screencap of "Welcome to River" page shows full dark theme. Launcher label reads "River" (notification permission dialog, All Apps drawer). Adaptive icon shows the dolphin logo.

content.subject: Investigate: rooms multiply on every Android launch
content.description:
Root cause: `example_data::create_room` generates fresh random `SigningKey`s every call, so `initial_rooms()` produced new owner_vks per launch. The chat-delegate save+load path persisted those random keys and merged them with the next launch's fresh set — same name, different HashMap key, both kept. 4 launches → 12 entries.

Fix committed: in `ui/src/components/app/chat_delegate.rs`, under `cfg(feature = "example-data")`, skip both `fire_load_rooms_request().await` in `set_up_chat_delegate` AND early-return `Ok(())` from `do_save_rooms_to_delegate`. Example-data builds now keep ROOMS purely in-memory per session.

Verified on Pixel 3a API 34 emulator: fresh install + 3 cold launches → exactly 3 rooms each time (Public Discussion Room, Team Chat Room, Your Private Room).

content.subject: Validate build-android-debug end-to-end on emulator
content.description: Debug APK built (52s, 3x faster than release) and installed on Pixel 3a API 34 emulator. Verified: launch → notification permission dialog renders dark; open room list → 3 example rooms (room-multiplication fix also works in debug); tap into Public Discussion Room → conversation view renders with messages; open members panel → list of members rendered; tap Eve Lopez → **member-info modal opens cleanly** (the exact previously-crashing spawn_local path at `member_info_modal.rs:181`). Zero `cannot access imported statics` / panic / SIGABRT in the entire session logcat. Debug builds are viable now that the spawn_local cleanup is complete — no upstream js-sys patches required.

# 3. Variant transforms (River = release / production; River Debug = debug).
#    Controlled by RIVER_VARIANT env var (default: release). The debug
#    variant ships side-by-side with release via a `.debug` applicationId
#    suffix, a distinct launcher label ("River Debug"), and an orange
#    adaptive-icon background so the two installs are visually
#    distinguishable on the home screen.
#
#    All edits write OVER the release-default files copied above, so the
#    release path is left untouched and any future overlay file change
#    lands first; the debug overrides come on top.
RIVER_VARIANT=${RIVER_VARIANT:-release}
echo "  Variant:         $RIVER_VARIANT"

case "$RIVER_VARIANT" in
    release)
        : # nothing to do — overlay defaults already are release
        ;;
    debug)
        # Launcher / activity label.
        cat > "$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml" <<'STRINGS_EOF'
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!--
  AUTO-GENERATED by scripts/apply-android-overlay.sh for RIVER_VARIANT=debug.
  Do not edit by hand — edit the heredoc in that script instead.
-->
<resources>
    <string name="app_name">River Debug</string>
</resources>
STRINGS_EOF

        # Adaptive-icon background color (Android 8+). For release we
        # keep the user-supplied solid-white WebP. For debug we swap the
        # adaptive-icon XML to point at a color resource and define that
        # color via colors.xml — same dolphin foreground, distinct
        # orange backdrop. Pre-API-26 fallback (the legacy
        # `mipmap-*/ic_launcher.webp`) is left as-is; the homescreen
        # launcher will use the round / squircle adaptive icon on every
        # device this side of 2018.
        cat > "$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/src/main/res/values/colors.xml" <<'COLORS_EOF'
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<resources>
    <color name="ic_launcher_background">#D97706</color>
</resources>
COLORS_EOF
        cat > "$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/src/main/res/mipmap-anydpi-v26/ic_launcher.xml" <<'ICON_EOF'
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<adaptive-icon xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android">
  <background android:drawable="@color/ic_launcher_background"/>
  <foreground android:drawable="@mipmap/ic_launcher_adaptive_fore"/>
</adaptive-icon>
ICON_EOF

        # applicationId suffix. dx writes `applicationId = "org.freenet.river"`
        # into build.gradle.kts on every regen. We rewrite to add a
        # `.debug` suffix so the debug APK installs side-by-side with
        # the release. The Kotlin namespace stays
        # `org.freenet.river` — that's the BuildConfig package, not the
        # install id. Idempotent: if the file already has `.debug`, the
        # regex doesn't match and the file is unchanged.
        perl -i -pe 's/applicationId\s*=\s*"org\.freenet\.river"$/applicationId = "org.freenet.river.debug"/' \
            "$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/build.gradle.kts"

        echo "  ✓ Applied debug variant transforms (label, icon color, applicationId .debug)"
        ;;
    *)
        echo "ERROR: unknown RIVER_VARIANT=$RIVER_VARIANT (expected 'release' or 'debug')" >&2
        exit 1
        ;;
esac

echo "Overlay applied successfully."

# files in `ui/android/`, and (b) re-apply them on top of the generated
# tree right before gradle assembles the APK. This script does (b).
#
# What it does (idempotent — safe to re-run on every build):
#   1. Copies every file under `ui/android/kotlin/` into the dx-generated
#      `src/main/kotlin/` directory, overwriting the stubs dx wrote there.
#   2. Patches `AndroidManifest.xml` to:
#      - Add `FOREGROUND_SERVICE` permission (INTERNET is already added
#        by dx).
#      - Add `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC` permission (required on
#        API 34+ for the `dataSync` foregroundServiceType; ignored on
#        older OS versions).
#      - Declare `<service android:name="dev.dioxus.main.RiverNodeService"
#        android:foregroundServiceType="dataSync" />` inside the
#        `<application>` element. `dataSync` is the closest stock
#        foreground-service type for a P2P node's background sync work
#        and is the only one compatible with the dx-generated
#        `compileSdk = 33`. If the project ever bumps compileSdk to 34+
#        we can switch to `specialUse` with a `freenet_p2p_node` subtype.
#
# The script writes only to `target/dx/`. It never touches `ui/android/`
# (the source-of-truth overlay) or anything outside the dx-generated
# Android module.

set -euo pipefail

# Where dx writes the Android module. Mirrors the path in
# `Makefile.toml`'s build-android task.
ANDROID_MODULE_DIR=${ANDROID_MODULE_DIR:-target/dx/river-ui/debug/android/app}
OVERLAY_DIR=${OVERLAY_DIR:-ui/android}

if [[ ! -d "$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR" ]]; then
    echo "ERROR: dx-generated Android module not found at $ANDROID_MODULE_DIR" >&2
    echo "       Run 'cargo make build-android' once to generate it, then re-run this script." >&2
    exit 1
fi

if [[ ! -d "$OVERLAY_DIR" ]]; then
    echo "ERROR: overlay source dir not found at $OVERLAY_DIR" >&2
    exit 1
fi

MANIFEST="$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml"
if [[ ! -f "$MANIFEST" ]]; then
    echo "ERROR: AndroidManifest.xml not found at $MANIFEST" >&2
    exit 1
fi

echo "Applying River Android overlay…"
echo "  Overlay source:  $OVERLAY_DIR"
echo "  Module target:   $ANDROID_MODULE_DIR"

# 1. Copy overlay Kotlin / resources into the generated module.
#    `cp -R` preserves the directory layout (so dev/dioxus/main/*.kt
#    lands at src/main/kotlin/dev/dioxus/main/*.kt).
if [[ -d "$OVERLAY_DIR/kotlin" ]]; then
    cp -R "$OVERLAY_DIR/kotlin/." "$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/src/main/kotlin/"
    echo "  ✓ Copied Kotlin overlay"
fi
if [[ -d "$OVERLAY_DIR/res" && -n "$(ls -A "$OVERLAY_DIR/res" 2>/dev/null)" ]]; then
    # For every file in our overlay tree, remove any same-basename file
    # in the target that has a DIFFERENT extension. Android's resource
    # merger treats `ic_launcher.png` and `ic_launcher.webp` in the same
    # density bucket as duplicates of the `ic_launcher` resource and
    # fails the build. The dx-generated tree ships defaults as .webp,
    # but a prior overlay run that placed .png files will leave them in
    # the target on subsequent builds (dx doesn't clean). This sweep
    # makes the overlay self-healing — pruning stale variants before
    # copying our canonical extension.
    while IFS= read -r -d '' overlay_file; do
        rel="${overlay_file#$OVERLAY_DIR/res/}"
        rel_dir=$(dirname "$rel")
        full_base=$(basename "$rel")
        base="${full_base%.*}"
        ext="${full_base##*.}"
        target_dir="$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/src/main/res/$rel_dir"
        if [[ -d "$target_dir" ]]; then
            for stale in "$target_dir/$base".*; do
                if [[ -f "$stale" && "${stale##*.}" != "$ext" ]]; then
                    rm "$stale"
                fi
            done
        fi
    done < <(find "$OVERLAY_DIR/res" -type f -print0)
    cp -R "$OVERLAY_DIR/res/." "$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/src/main/res/"
    echo "  ✓ Copied res overlay (pruned stale duplicate-extension variants)"
fi

# 2. Patch the manifest. Each insertion is idempotent — we grep for
#    the entry first and only add if missing. This means re-running the
#    script after dx has regenerated a fresh manifest produces the same
#    result as running it the first time.
patch_manifest() {
    local pattern=$1
    local before=$2
    local insertion=$3

    if grep -q -F "$pattern" "$MANIFEST"; then
        return 0
    fi

    # Insert `$insertion` on the line BEFORE `$before`. macOS sed needs
    # the -i '' form; we use a portable Perl invocation instead so the
    # script runs the same on macOS and Linux CI.
    perl -i -pe "s|($before)|$insertion\n\$1|" "$MANIFEST"
}

# Add FOREGROUND_SERVICE + FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC permissions.
# We grep-test for each by full string so re-runs are no-ops.
patch_manifest \
    'android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE"' \
    '<application ' \
    '    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE" />'
patch_manifest \
    'android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC"' \
    '<application ' \
    '    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC" />'

# POST_NOTIFICATIONS is required on API 33+ for the foreground-service
# notification to be visible in the status bar. Without it the FGS still
# runs (Android allows the process to keep executing) but the user sees
# nothing — defeating the "ongoing presence" UX of the service.
# This is a runtime permission too: the user must grant it on first
# launch. The MainActivity overlay requests it via PermissionHelper.
patch_manifest \
    'android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS"' \
    '<application ' \
    '    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS" />'

# Declare the service inside <application>. Inserted on the line BEFORE
# `</application>` so the closing tag remains intact.
patch_manifest \
    '"dev.dioxus.main.RiverNodeService"' \
    '</application>' \
    '        <service android:name="dev.dioxus.main.RiverNodeService" android:exported="false" android:foregroundServiceType="dataSync" />'

echo "  ✓ Patched AndroidManifest.xml"
echo "Overlay applied successfully."

#!/bin/bash
set -e
export ANDROID_HOME="${ANDROID_HOME:-$HOME/Library/Android/sdk}"
export ANDROID_NDK_HOME="${ANDROID_NDK_HOME:-$(ls -d "$ANDROID_HOME"/ndk/* 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -1)}"
echo "ANDROID_HOME=$ANDROID_HOME"
echo "ANDROID_NDK_HOME=$ANDROID_NDK_HOME"

# Stage 1: dx generates the Android module, compiles the Rust native
# lib, and invokes gradle. The first APK exists at this point but
# doesn't carry our Kotlin overlay (RiverNodeService + the MainActivity
# that starts it). dx regenerates AndroidManifest.xml and the
# MainActivity stub every build, so we can't inject before gradle —
# we overlay and re-build.
#
# Profile is selected by the calling task via DX_RELEASE_FLAG +
# DX_OUT_DIR env vars (see [tasks.build-android] vs
# [tasks.build-android-debug] in this file).
#
# Historical note (commit 39652562) said release was REQUIRED to avoid
# wasm-bindgen-futures' `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]` `CREATE_TASK`
# extern (js-sys-0.3.99/src/futures/task/singlethread.rs:22 —
# `cannot access imported statics on non-wasm targets`). The extern
# IS still emitted in debug builds, but it only panics when a code
# path actually reads `CREATE_TASK` via `Task::spawn` /
# `wasm_bindgen_futures::spawn_local`. Once every non-cfg-gated
# bare callsite was rerouted through `crate::util::safe_spawn_local`
# (commits e58c3c38 + bd1a7d0d), the read no longer happens on
# Android and debug builds are viable again — see
# [tasks.build-android-debug].
( cd ui && dx build $DX_RELEASE_FLAG --platform android --features example-data )

# dx puts profile-tagged output under `target/dx/river-ui/<profile>`,
# matching whichever profile flag was passed. Stage 2 + 3 must target
# that same tree so the overlay rsync lands on the Rust binary we
# just compiled.
ANDROID_MODULE_DIR=target/dx/river-ui/$DX_OUT_DIR/android/app

# Stage 2: copy `ui/android/` (canonical overlay) over the generated
# module and patch the manifest. Idempotent — safe on every build.
ANDROID_MODULE_DIR="$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR" scripts/apply-android-overlay.sh

# Stage 3: re-invoke gradle so the patched manifest + new Kotlin
# sources land in the APK. Incremental: only the changed files trigger
# work, so this stage is much faster than the first one.
( cd "$ANDROID_MODULE_DIR" && ./gradlew :app:assembleDebug )

echo ""
echo "APK: $ANDROID_MODULE_DIR/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk"
'''

content.description: Verified on Pixel 10 Pro XL after building + installing the patched APK: user confirmed "The Copy button works!" The JNI bridge in `ui/src/util.rs::android_copy_to_clipboard` (mirrors the `node_runtime::android_files_dir` pattern — pull JavaVM+Activity from ndk_context, attach thread, reflect Context.getSystemService("clipboard") → ClipData.newPlainText → setPrimaryClip) correctly writes the text into the system clipboard, where the user could paste it. Pre-fix behaviour was a no-op `let _ = text;` that silently swallowed every Copy.

content.subject: Fix GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed in nickname-save chain
content.description:
Pre-existing crash surfaced during Android verification on Pixel 10 Pro XL. Panic at `dioxus-signals-0.7.9/src/global/mod.rs:100:46` ("called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: AlreadyBorrowed(AlreadyBorrowedError)") on a nickname edit + Enter.

Sequence from logcat (`/tmp/claude/river-logcat.txt`, line 5569):
1. `Sending PutRequest for room MemberId(K53VLDBK)` (room_synchronizer.rs)
2. `Saving rooms to delegate storage` (chat_delegate.rs)
3. `Serialized request payload size: 131383 bytes`
4. Panic — `thread 'main' (4707) panicked at .../global/mod.rs:100:46`
5. SIGABRT

`nickname_field.rs::save_changes` already wraps its `ROOMS.with_mut` in `crate::util::defer`, so the immediate save delta is safe. The re-entrant borrow must be in the downstream chain triggered by `mark_needs_sync(owner_key)` — likely `save_rooms_to_delegate` reading a GlobalSignal while another mutation is still borrowed. Audit `save_rooms_to_delegate` and any use_effect / use_memo it triggers for unwrapped GlobalSignal reads (per AGENTS.md "Always use try_read()" rule).

Reproduction: edit a nickname in member-info modal, press Enter on Android (Pixel 10 Pro XL, current build). Unverified if web is affected.
content.activeForm: Pending: GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed in nickname save

content.subject: Move misleading "Saving nickname changes" log into closure body
content.description:
`nickname_field.rs:60` has `info!("Saving nickname changes");` inside the closure-creation block (around `let save_changes = { info!(...); ... move |new_value| { ... } }`), so it fires on every component re-render — i.e. every keystroke in the nickname input — not on actual saves. The 30+ log entries we saw in the verification logcat were all spurious re-renders, not actual save attempts.

Fix: move the `info!` inside the `move |new_value: String| { ... }` block so it only fires when `save_changes(new_value)` is actually called from `on_blur` or `on_keydown(Enter)`. Cosmetic but the noise actively obscures real save activity in logs (and confused the initial diagnosis of the GlobalSignal crash above).

Probe via injected JS showed pcs:true, metas:1, bg:rgb(10,10,11) — confirming `prefers-color-scheme: dark` matches and the body bg is the `--color-bg: #0a0a0b` token from tailwind.css's dark block. content.subject: Investigate: rooms multiply on every Android launch
content.description:
Root cause: `example_data::create_room` generates fresh random `SigningKey`s every call, so `initial_rooms()` produced new owner_vks per launch. The chat-delegate save+load path persisted those random keys and merged them with the next launch's fresh set — same name, different HashMap key, both kept. 4 launches → 12 entries.

Fix committed: in `ui/src/components/app/chat_delegate.rs`, under `cfg(feature = "example-data")`, skip both `fire_load_rooms_request().await` in `set_up_chat_delegate` AND early-return `Ok(())` from `do_save_rooms_to_delegate`. Example-data builds now keep ROOMS purely in-memory per session.

Verified on Pixel 3a API 34 emulator: fresh install + 3 cold launches → exactly 3 rooms each time (Public Discussion Room, Team Chat Room, Your Private Room).

content.subject: Validate build-android-debug end-to-end on emulator
content.description: Debug APK built (52s, 3x faster than release) and installed on Pixel 3a API 34 emulator. Verified: launch → notification permission dialog renders dark; open room list → 3 example rooms (room-multiplication fix also works in debug); tap into Public Discussion Room → conversation view renders with messages; open members panel → list of members rendered; tap Eve Lopez → **member-info modal opens cleanly** (the exact previously-crashing spawn_local path at `member_info_modal.rs:181`). Zero `cannot access imported statics` / panic / SIGABRT in the entire session logcat. Debug builds are viable now that the spawn_local cleanup is complete — no upstream js-sys patches required.

content.text:
I see a `Failed NAT traversal ... max connection attempts reached peer_addr=100.27.151.80:31337` in the logs — but I want to understand what step is failing. Can you describe what you see when you try to join? Specifically:

- Are you using the **Join via Invitation** button (paste a URL/code)?
- Does the paste modal open?
- After you paste + tap join, does the **Receive Invitation** modal appear?
- Does the room briefly appear and disappear, or never appear at all?

While I wait, a hypothesis I want to verify: my room-multiplication fix made the chat-delegate `rooms_data` save into a no-op under `example-data`. That's fine for example rooms (they're in-memory), but a **real** room joined via invitation in the debug build would also be ephemeral — and worse, anything that requires the delegate to know about the room's signing key may fail. Let me check the join path.

content.subject: Fix GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed in nickname-save chain
content.description:
Pre-existing crash surfaced during Android verification on Pixel 10 Pro XL. Panic at `dioxus-signals-0.7.9/src/global/mod.rs:100:46` ("called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: AlreadyBorrowed(AlreadyBorrowedError)") on a nickname edit + Enter.

Sequence from logcat (`/tmp/claude/river-logcat.txt`, line 5569):
1. `Sending PutRequest for room MemberId(K53VLDBK)` (room_synchronizer.rs)
2. `Saving rooms to delegate storage` (chat_delegate.rs)
3. `Serialized request payload size: 131383 bytes`
4. Panic — `thread 'main' (4707) panicked at .../global/mod.rs:100:46`
5. SIGABRT

`nickname_field.rs::save_changes` already wraps its `ROOMS.with_mut` in `crate::util::defer`, so the immediate save delta is safe. The re-entrant borrow must be in the downstream chain triggered by `mark_needs_sync(owner_key)` — likely `save_rooms_to_delegate` reading a GlobalSignal while another mutation is still borrowed. Audit `save_rooms_to_delegate` and any use_effect / use_memo it triggers for unwrapped GlobalSignal reads (per AGENTS.md "Always use try_read()" rule).

Reproduction: edit a nickname in member-info modal, press Enter on Android (Pixel 10 Pro XL, current build). Unverified if web is affected.
content.activeForm: Pending: GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed in nickname save

content.subject: Move misleading "Saving nickname changes" log into closure body
content.description:
`nickname_field.rs:60` has `info!("Saving nickname changes");` inside the closure-creation block (around `let save_changes = { info!(...); ... move |new_value| { ... } }`), so it fires on every component re-render — i.e. every keystroke in the nickname input — not on actual saves. The 30+ log entries we saw in the verification logcat were all spurious re-renders, not actual save attempts.

Fix: move the `info!` inside the `move |new_value: String| { ... }` block so it only fires when `save_changes(new_value)` is actually called from `on_blur` or `on_keydown(Enter)`. Cosmetic but the noise actively obscures real save activity in logs (and confused the initial diagnosis of the GlobalSignal crash above).

content.subject: Investigate: rooms multiply on every Android launch
content.description:
Root cause: `example_data::create_room` generates fresh random `SigningKey`s every call, so `initial_rooms()` produced new owner_vks per launch. The chat-delegate save+load path persisted those random keys and merged them with the next launch's fresh set — same name, different HashMap key, both kept. 4 launches → 12 entries.

Fix committed: in `ui/src/components/app/chat_delegate.rs`, under `cfg(feature = "example-data")`, skip both `fire_load_rooms_request().await` in `set_up_chat_delegate` AND early-return `Ok(())` from `do_save_rooms_to_delegate`. Example-data builds now keep ROOMS purely in-memory per session.

Verified on Pixel 3a API 34 emulator: fresh install + 3 cold launches → exactly 3 rooms each time (Public Discussion Room, Team Chat Room, Your Private Room).

content.text: Want to ask you specifically what's happening, but also a hypothesis worth testing: **both apps are running their own embedded Freenet node simultaneously** (the debug FGS notification is alongside the release one). content.text: Both fail → not a debug-specific bug. The embedded node's NAT traversal is failing (per the logcat error from earlier). Likely cause: **both apps running embedded Freenet nodes simultaneously** are competing for ports / both trying to do UDP hole-punching from behind the same NAT. Let me test by killing one and retrying.

content.text:
**Root cause identified — and it's NOT about the debug variant or my recent changes.**

The Rust log says:

```
freenet::client_events: Operation rejected: peer has not joined network yet - client should retry after join
river_ui: WebSocket connection error: client error: peer has not joined the network yet
```

The embedded Freenet node is **up but hasn't bootstrapped onto the network yet** (NAT traversal to the gateway is failing). When you paste the invitation and tap Join, the node says "I'm not on the network, can't fetch a room contract." The UI's Receive Invitation modal sits at "subscribing" because the GET request errors out immediately.

The earlier logcat line — `Failed NAT traversal ... max connection attempts reached peer_addr=100.27.151.80:31337` (nova gateway) — is the underlying failure. This is the SAME intermittent gateway-unreachable issue we hit earlier today (documented in `openspec/changes/android-bundled-node/tasks.md` task 3.5).

Let me check whether the node ever connects, and whether the WiFi-side path to nova actually works.

content.text:
## Diagnosis: it's the network, not the app

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Logcat for River release after relaunch | **No peer connections at all** in 20s wait |
| `nc -zvuw3 100.27.151.80 31337` from this Mac | ✅ succeeded (nova gateway reachable) |
| `nc -zvuw3 5.9.111.215 31337` from this Mac | ✅ succeeded (vega gateway reachable) |
| Phone's Wi-Fi SSID | `CHLwelcome` |

Both gateways are up — but the phone's embedded Freenet node can't NAT-traverse to them. The Mac on the same Wi-Fi reaches them with simple UDP, but Freenet's NAT-traversal handshake needs the public network to cooperate with timing-sensitive UDP hole-punching, which **`CHLwelcome` (a public/guest Wi-Fi)** typically blocks via symmetric NAT and short UDP-binding timeouts.

The error chain:
1. Embedded node tries to connect to nova → `Failed NAT traversal max connection attempts reached`
2. Node never reports "peer connection established"
3. You paste invitation, tap Join → River sends `GetRequest` for the room contract
4. freenet-core: `"peer has not joined network yet"` → returns error
5. UI's Receive Invitation modal hangs at "subscribing"

**This is NOT caused by**: the debug variant, the room-multiplication fix, the two-nodes-fighting hypothesis (River Debug is killed and River alone still can't connect), or any of today's commits. It's network-level — the Pixel behind this Wi-Fi can't NAT-traverse.

**What to try:**
- Switch the phone to **mobile data** (turn off Wi-Fi) — different NAT path
- Switch to a **different Wi-Fi** (home / hotspot / less restrictive guest)
- Same invitation will work as soon as the embedded node manages to bootstrap (you'll see `NAT traversal connection established` in logcat)

Want me to verify by having you toggle the phone to mobile data and re-test, or is that something you'd rather just do whenever you're back on a friendly network?

content.subject: Fix GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed in nickname-save chain
content.description:
Pre-existing crash surfaced during Android verification on Pixel 10 Pro XL. Panic at `dioxus-signals-0.7.9/src/global/mod.rs:100:46` ("called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: AlreadyBorrowed(AlreadyBorrowedError)") on a nickname edit + Enter.

Sequence from logcat (`/tmp/claude/river-logcat.txt`, line 5569):
1. `Sending PutRequest for room MemberId(K53VLDBK)` (room_synchronizer.rs)
2. `Saving rooms to delegate storage` (chat_delegate.rs)
3. `Serialized request payload size: 131383 bytes`
4. Panic — `thread 'main' (4707) panicked at .../global/mod.rs:100:46`
5. SIGABRT

`nickname_field.rs::save_changes` already wraps its `ROOMS.with_mut` in `crate::util::defer`, so the immediate save delta is safe. The re-entrant borrow must be in the downstream chain triggered by `mark_needs_sync(owner_key)` — likely `save_rooms_to_delegate` reading a GlobalSignal while another mutation is still borrowed. Audit `save_rooms_to_delegate` and any use_effect / use_memo it triggers for unwrapped GlobalSignal reads (per AGENTS.md "Always use try_read()" rule).

Reproduction: edit a nickname in member-info modal, press Enter on Android (Pixel 10 Pro XL, current build). Unverified if web is affected.

content.subject: Move misleading "Saving nickname changes" log into closure body
content.description:
`nickname_field.rs:60` has `info!("Saving nickname changes");` inside the closure-creation block (around `let save_changes = { info!(...); ... move |new_value| { ... } }`), so it fires on every component re-render — i.e. every keystroke in the nickname input — not on actual saves. The 30+ log entries we saw in the verification logcat were all spurious re-renders, not actual save attempts.

Fix: move the `info!` inside the `move |new_value: String| { ... }` block so it only fires when `save_changes(new_value)` is actually called from `on_blur` or `on_keydown(Enter)`. Cosmetic but the noise actively obscures real save activity in logs (and confused the initial diagnosis of the GlobalSignal crash above).

content.subject: Investigate: rooms multiply on every Android launch
content.description:
Root cause: `example_data::create_room` generates fresh random `SigningKey`s every call, so `initial_rooms()` produced new owner_vks per launch. The chat-delegate save+load path persisted those random keys and merged them with the next launch's fresh set — same name, different HashMap key, both kept. 4 launches → 12 entries.

Fix committed: in `ui/src/components/app/chat_delegate.rs`, under `cfg(feature = "example-data")`, skip both `fire_load_rooms_request().await` in `set_up_chat_delegate` AND early-return `Ok(())` from `do_save_rooms_to_delegate`. Example-data builds now keep ROOMS purely in-memory per session.

Verified on Pixel 3a API 34 emulator: fresh install + 3 cold launches → exactly 3 rooms each time (Public Discussion Room, Team Chat Room, Your Private Room).

- Any public Wi-Fi that isn't running symmetric NAT (most coffee shops, libraries — but NOT this `CHLwelcome` you were on)

Worth filing upstream though — Freenet really should ship IPv6 gateways and/or a TURN relay so users behind CGNAT (which is most mobile carriers now) aren't stranded. Want me to file that as a freenet-core issue while we wait for you to be on a friendly network?

## Confirmed: gateways are unreachable from this Wi-Fi *right now*

From my **Mac** on the same `CHLwelcome` Wi-Fi as the phone:
- `ping 100.27.151.80` (nova) → **100% packet loss**
- UDP echo test to nova `:31337` → **no response**
- UDP echo test to vega `5.9.111.215:31337` → **no response**

Not a CGNAT issue, not a debug-build issue, not the two-nodes-fighting issue. **The gateway IPs are firewalled / unreachable from this Wi-Fi at this moment.**

My earlier `nc -zvuw3` "succeeded" reading was misleading — `nc -z` with UDP only confirms the local socket send didn't fail; it doesn't wait for a reply. The proper bidirectional test above shows nothing comes back.

Earlier today the phone genuinely did peer-up on this same Wi-Fi (openspec doc records `active_peers=5`). So something has changed since then — gateway rate-limit, Wi-Fi DPI rule, or transient gateway downtime. Try a hotspot or different Wi-Fi.

content.text:
That maps to a UX gap, not a bug. From the logcat:

- **`active_connections=0`** every time the node tries to send. The node has *never* reached an active peer connection in the current session.
- River's UI shows a message as "sent" the moment the local PUT request is dispatched — it doesn't distinguish "broadcast to peers and persisted in the contract" from "queued locally because there's no peer to send to."

So messages you typed during a span when the node was disconnected would appear sent locally but never actually leave the device. Conversely, the fact that you *saw* messages from others means the node DID connect at some point during the session and pulled the room contract state.

**Two quick ways to confirm what actually went out:**

1. **Check the room from another peer** — open the same room from your web River session, or have someone else who's in the room scroll back to see if your messages showed up. If they're there, your sends made it out before the connection dropped.
2. **In the current session, the answer is "no"** — any send you do right now sits in a queue and dies with the process, because there's no peer to push it through.

Worth filing as a UX issue: **River should distinguish "queued" / "sent" / "confirmed by N peers" in the message bubble**. Today's UI conflates "I dispatched the PUT" with "the message is on the network." Want me to file that?

Side note: it's been ~15 minutes since the node tried to reach the gateways and it's still at 0 connections — `CHLwelcome` Wi-Fi is genuinely not routing UDP to those public IPs right now. Your earlier joined-room state is from a session where the path DID work briefly.

content.subject: Move misleading "Saving nickname changes" log into closure body
content.description:
`nickname_field.rs:60` has `info!("Saving nickname changes");` inside the closure-creation block (around `let save_changes = { info!(...); ... move |new_value| { ... } }`), so it fires on every component re-render — i.e. every keystroke in the nickname input — not on actual saves. The 30+ log entries we saw in the verification logcat were all spurious re-renders, not actual save attempts.

Fix: move the `info!` inside the `move |new_value: String| { ... }` block so it only fires when `save_changes(new_value)` is actually called from `on_blur` or `on_keydown(Enter)`. Cosmetic but the noise actively obscures real save activity in logs (and confused the initial diagnosis of the GlobalSignal crash above).

content.subject: Investigate: rooms multiply on every Android launch
content.description:
Root cause: `example_data::create_room` generates fresh random `SigningKey`s every call, so `initial_rooms()` produced new owner_vks per launch. The chat-delegate save+load path persisted those random keys and merged them with the next launch's fresh set — same name, different HashMap key, both kept. 4 launches → 12 entries.

Fix committed: in `ui/src/components/app/chat_delegate.rs`, under `cfg(feature = "example-data")`, skip both `fire_load_rooms_request().await` in `set_up_chat_delegate` AND early-return `Ok(())` from `do_save_rooms_to_delegate`. Example-data builds now keep ROOMS purely in-memory per session.

Verified on Pixel 3a API 34 emulator: fresh install + 3 cold launches → exactly 3 rooms each time (Public Discussion Room, Team Chat Room, Your Private Room).

content.subject: Verify join works on mobile data (network-environment retest)
content.description:
Confirmed bootstrap failure is NETWORK-LEVEL, not code:

- Phone (River release + River Debug builds) on CHLwelcome Wi-Fi: 0 peer connections, 12-attempt UDP handshake times out against both bundled gateways (nova 100.27.151.80:31337, vega 5.9.111.215:31337).
- Mac on the SAME CHLwelcome Wi-Fi: `ping 100.27.151.80` → 100% packet loss; UDP echo test to both gateways → no response.

- Earlier today the same Pixel did connect from this Wi-Fi (openspec doc shows active_peers=5). So the gateway path was working then; some combination of Wi-Fi firewall rule change, gateway rate-limiting on this Wi-Fi's public IP, or transient gateway downtime is dropping the path now.

User remedy: switch to a hotspot or non-CHLwelcome Wi-Fi.
Upstream remedy: freenet-core should ship IPv6 gateways and/or a TURN-style relay path so users on hostile NAT / firewalled Wi-Fi aren't fully stranded.

content.subject: Fix GlobalSignal AlreadyBorrowed in nickname-save chain
content.description:
Pre-existing crash surfaced during Android verification on Pixel 10 Pro XL. Panic at `dioxus-signals-0.7.9/src/global/mod.rs:100:46` ("called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: AlreadyBorrowed(AlreadyBorrowedError)") on a nickname edit + Enter.

Sequence from logcat (`/tmp/claude/river-logcat.txt`, line 5569):
1. `Sending PutRequest for room MemberId(K53VLDBK)` (room_synchronizer.rs)
2. `Saving rooms to delegate storage` (chat_delegate.rs)
3. `Serialized request payload size: 131383 bytes`
4. Panic — `thread 'main' (4707) panicked at .../global/mod.rs:100:46`
5. SIGABRT

`nickname_field.rs::save_changes` already wraps its `ROOMS.with_mut` in `crate::util::defer`, so the immediate save delta is safe. The re-entrant borrow must be in the downstream chain triggered by `mark_needs_sync(owner_key)` — likely `save_rooms_to_delegate` reading a GlobalSignal while another mutation is still borrowed. Audit `save_rooms_to_delegate` and any use_effect / use_memo it triggers for unwrapped GlobalSignal reads (per AGENTS.md "Always use try_read()" rule).

Reproduction: edit a nickname in member-info modal, press Enter on Android (Pixel 10 Pro XL, current build). Unverified if web is affected.

content.subject: Move misleading "Saving nickname changes" log into closure body
content.description:
`nickname_field.rs:60` has `info!("Saving nickname changes");` inside the closure-creation block (around `let save_changes = { info!(...); ... move |new_value| { ... } }`), so it fires on every component re-render — i.e. every keystroke in the nickname input — not on actual saves. The 30+ log entries we saw in the verification logcat were all spurious re-renders, not actual save attempts.

Fix: move the `info!` inside the `move |new_value: String| { ... }` block so it only fires when `save_changes(new_value)` is actually called from `on_blur` or `on_keydown(Enter)`. Cosmetic but the noise actively obscures real save activity in logs (and confused the initial diagnosis of the GlobalSignal crash above).

content.subject: Investigate: rooms multiply on every Android launch
content.description:
Root cause: `example_data::create_room` generates fresh random `SigningKey`s every call, so `initial_rooms()` produced new owner_vks per launch. The chat-delegate save+load path persisted those random keys and merged them with the next launch's fresh set — same name, different HashMap key, both kept. 4 launches → 12 entries.

Fix committed: in `ui/src/components/app/chat_delegate.rs`, under `cfg(feature = "example-data")`, skip both `fire_load_rooms_request().await` in `set_up_chat_delegate` AND early-return `Ok(())` from `do_save_rooms_to_delegate`. Example-data builds now keep ROOMS purely in-memory per session.

Verified on Pixel 3a API 34 emulator: fresh install + 3 cold launches → exactly 3 rooms each time (Public Discussion Room, Team Chat Room, Your Private Room).

content.subject: Verify join works on mobile data (network-environment retest)
content.description:
Confirmed bootstrap failure is NETWORK-LEVEL, not code:

- Phone (River release + River Debug builds) on CHLwelcome Wi-Fi: 0 peer connections, 12-attempt UDP handshake times out against both bundled gateways (nova 100.27.151.80:31337, vega 5.9.111.215:31337).
- Mac on the SAME CHLwelcome Wi-Fi: `ping 100.27.151.80` → 100% packet loss; UDP echo test to both gateways → no response.
- Mac on phone's mobile data path is N/A (mobile data is AT&T CGNAT — phone can't even ICMP-ping gateway).
- Earlier today the same Pixel did connect from this Wi-Fi (openspec doc shows active_peers=5). So the gateway path was working then; some combination of Wi-Fi firewall rule change, gateway rate-limiting on this Wi-Fi's public IP, or transient gateway downtime is dropping the path now.

User remedy: switch to a hotspot or non-CHLwelcome Wi-Fi.
Upstream remedy: freenet-core should ship IPv6 gateways and/or a TURN-style relay path so users on hostile NAT / firewalled Wi-Fi aren't fully stranded.

git add Makefile.toml scripts/apply-android-overlay.sh
git commit -m "feat(android): split into River (release) + River Debug (dev) variants

build-android: release Rust profile, no example-data, installs as
  org.freenet.river ('River'), preserves the user-supplied dolphin
  launcher icon.
build-android-debug: dev Rust profile (~3x faster compile), with
  example-data, installs as org.freenet.river.debug ('River Debug'),
  orange (#D97706) adaptive-icon background, side-by-side with
  release.

Wired via DX_RELEASE_FLAG / DX_OUT_DIR / DX_FEATURES / RIVER_VARIANT
env vars set by the calling task; the overlay script branches on
RIVER_VARIANT to rewrite strings.xml, colors.xml,
mipmap-anydpi-v26/ic_launcher.xml, and patches build.gradle.kts's
applicationId.

Verified on Pixel 10 Pro XL: both APKs install simultaneously
(pm list packages shows both ids), each launches its own
RiverNodeService FGS, each has its own private files dir.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>"

# 3. Receive Invitation loading bar (#30)
git add ui/src/components/room_list/receive_invitation_modal.rs
git commit -m "feat(ui): receive-invitation loading bar reflects real progress

Replace the fixed-width pulse with two CSS @keyframe animations that
genuinely fill over the underlying timeouts:

  - PendingSubscription: 10% -> 35% over 3s (state usually transitions
    through in <1s; subtle 'something's happening' indicator).
  - Subscribing: 35% -> 92% over INVITATION_TIMEOUT_MS (90s, single
    source of truth — the synchronizer resets back to
    PendingSubscription at that exact threshold for a retry, and the
    style re-mounts on each status flip so the bar restarts visibly).

Bar caps at 92%, never claims 'done' until the GET actually returns.

Adds a sub-line under the bar surfacing SYNC_STATUS so a stuck
local-node WebSocket is visible ('Connecting to local Freenet node…' /
